questions.prompt: After Chapter 9 shows that structure can limit results, what does Chapter 10 add?
choices: How to design choices into a reinforcing whole
How to improve every part equally
How to avoid choosing among good options
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 moves from structural diagnosis to design, asking how choices should work together as a whole.

questions.prompt: What makes a designed strategy different from a pile of good moves?
choices: Each move is individually impressive
The moves reinforce one another
The plan contains the most activity
questions.explanation: Design is about fit and mutual reinforcement, not about accumulating attractive moves.

choices: Treating exclusion as part of coherence
Assuming isolated strengths automatically make a strong whole
Testing whether choices fit the obstacle
questions.explanation: The chapter argues that respectable parts can still form a weak strategy if they do not fit together.

questions.prompt: A school team has many exciting showcase ideas, but they clash in timing and purpose. What is the Chapter 10 diagnosis?
choices: The plan needs more features
The plan lacks structural fit and reinforcement
The team should judge each part alone
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 asks whether the pieces form a coherent whole rather than merely sounding attractive separately.

questions.prompt: Why can exclusion strengthen a strategy?
choices: Because fewer choices are always morally better
Because cutting conflicting moves can preserve reinforcement
Because strategy should avoid commitment
questions.explanation: Some attractive options need to stay outside the design so the remaining choices can reinforce one another.

choices: By ignoring structural limits once they are found
By turning diagnosis of limits into design of a coherent whole
By replacing structure with motivation
questions.explanation: Chapter 9 identifies structural limits; Chapter 10 asks how to build choices that work together under those conditions.

questions.prompt: A household routine only improves after the steps are rearranged so each one helps the next. What concept is this showing?
choices: Mutual reinforcement inside a design
Average strength across many parts
Avoidance of difficult tradeoffs
questions.explanation: The routine gets stronger because the parts fit together and reinforce one another.

questions.prompt: What is the best sign that a strategy has structural fit?
choices: The choices support the same logic and strengthen one another
The plan contains many independently good ideas
The team refuses to remove any option
questions.explanation: Fit shows up when choices align with the obstacle, the constraints, and each other.

questions.prompt: Why can more activity still weaken the whole?
choices: Because activity is never useful
Because additional moves can dilute fit and divide effort
Because fewer choices always guarantee success
questions.explanation: A longer list can make the strategy weaker when new moves conflict with or distract from the reinforcing structure.

questions.prompt: Why does Chapter 10 naturally lead into a chapter on focus?
choices: Because a designed whole still has to decide where concentration belongs
Because design removes the need for prioritization
Because every strong plan should reinforce everything equally
questions.explanation: Once the whole is designed, the next question is where that whole should concentrate its force rather than spread it everywhere.
